# dlar1v

> Compute the (scaled) `r`-th column of the inverse of the submatrix in rows `b1` through `bn` of the tridiagonal matrix `L*D*L^T - lambda*I`.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dlar1v from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dlar1v';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dlar1v(
    N,
    b1, bn, lambda,
    D, strideD,
    L, strideL,
    LD, strideLD,
    LLD, strideLLD,
    pivmin, gaptol,
    Z, strideZ,
    wantnc,
    negcnt,
    ztz,
    mingma,
    r,
    ISUPPZ, strideISUPPZ,
    nrminv,
    resid,
    rqcorr,
    WORK
) → Int32Array
```

Computes the (scaled) `r`-th column of the inverse of the submatrix in rows `b1` through `bn` of the tridiagonal matrix `L*D*L^T - lambda*I`.

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | order of the matrix |
| `b1` | `integer` | in |  |  | (1-based) first index of the submatrix |
| `bn` | `integer` | in |  |  | (1-based) last index of the submatrix |
| `lambda` | `number` | in |  |  | shift (approximate eigenvalue) |
| `D` | `Float64Array` | in | `N` |  | diagonal of `L*D*L^T` |
| ↳ `strideD` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `D` |
| `L` | `Float64Array` | in | `N - 1` |  | sub-diagonal of the unit lower bidiagonal factor |
| ↳ `strideL` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `L` |
| `LD` | `Float64Array` | in | `N - 1` |  | element-wise product `L*D` |
| ↳ `strideLD` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `LD` |
| `LLD` | `Float64Array` | in | `N - 1` |  | element-wise product `L*D*L` |
| ↳ `strideLLD` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `LLD` |
| `pivmin` | `number` | in |  |  | minimum pivot in the Sturm sequence |
| `gaptol` | `number` | in |  |  | tolerance that determines when a column of the inverse has converged |
| `Z` | `Float64Array` | in/out | `N` |  | output eigenvector (length `N`) |
| ↳ `strideZ` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `Z` |
| `wantnc` | `boolean` | in |  |  | if `true`, compute `negcnt` |
| `negcnt` | `Int32Array` | out |  |  | output (length >= 1) |
| `ztz` | `Float64Array` | out |  |  | output (length >= 1) |
| `mingma` | `Float64Array` | out |  |  | output (length >= 1) |
| `r` | `Int32Array` | in/out |  |  | in/out (length >= 1) |
| `ISUPPZ` | `Int32Array` | out | `2` |  | output (length >= 2) |
| ↳ `strideISUPPZ` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `ISUPPZ` |
| `nrminv` | `Float64Array` | out |  |  | output (length >= 1) |
| `resid` | `Float64Array` | out |  |  | output (length >= 1) |
| `rqcorr` | `Float64Array` | out |  |  | output (length >= 1) |
| `WORK` | `(Float64Array\|null)` | out | `≥ 4 * N` |  | workspace (length >= 4*N) |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `N`: The order of the matrix L D $L^T$.
- `b1`: First index of the submatrix of L D $L^T$.
- `bn`: Last index of the submatrix of L D $L^T$.
- `lambda`: The shift. In order to compute an accurate eigenvector, `LAMBDA` should be a good approximation to an eigenvalue of L D $L^T$.
- `D`: The n diagonal elements of the diagonal matrix D.
- `L`: The (n-1) subdiagonal elements of the unit bidiagonal matrix L, in elements 1 to N-1.
- `LD`: The n-1 elements $L(i) \, D(i)$.
- `LLD`: The n-1 elements $L(i) \, L(i) \, D(i)$.
- `pivmin`: The minimum pivot in the Sturm sequence.
- `gaptol`: Tolerance that indicates when eigenvector entries are negligible w.r.t. their contribution to the residual.
- `Z`: On input, all entries of Z must be set to 0. On output, Z contains the (scaled) r-th column of the inverse. The scaling is such that `Z(R)` equals 1.
- `wantnc`: Specifies whether `NEGCNT` has to be computed.
- `negcnt`: If `WANTNC` is .TRUE. then `NEGCNT` = the number of pivots \< pivmin in the matrix factorization L D $L^T$, and `NEGCNT = -1` otherwise.
- `ztz`: The square of the 2-norm of Z.
- `mingma`: The reciprocal of the largest (in magnitude) diagonal element of the inverse of L D $L^T - \sigma$ I.
- `r`: The twist index for the twisted factorization used to compute Z. On input, $0 \le R \le N$. If R is input as 0, R is set to the index where $(L D L^T - \sigma I)$^{-1} is largest in magnitude. If $1 \le R \le N$, R is unchanged. On output, R contains the twist index used to compute Z. Ideally, R designates the position of the maximum entry in the eigenvector.
- `ISUPPZ`: The support of the vector in Z, i.e., the vector Z is nonzero only in elements `ISUPPZ(1)` through ISUPPZ( 2 ).
- `nrminv`: $\mathrm{NRMINV} = 1/\sqrt{ \mathrm{ZTZ} }$
- `resid`: The residual of the FP vector. $\mathrm{RESID} = \lvert \mathrm{MINGMA} \rvert/\sqrt{ \mathrm{ZTZ} }$
- `rqcorr`: The Rayleigh Quotient correction to `LAMBDA`. $\mathrm{RQCORR} = \mathrm{MINGMA} \, \mathrm{TMP}$

</details>

**Returns** `Int32Array`

**Throws**

- `RangeError` first argument must be a nonnegative integer

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dlar1v.ndarray(
    N,
    b1, bn, lambda,
    D, strideD, offsetD,
    L, strideL, offsetL,
    LD, strideLD, offsetLD,
    LLD, strideLLD, offsetLLD,
    pivmin, gaptol,
    Z, strideZ, offsetZ,
    wantnc,
    negcnt,
    ztz,
    mingma,
    r,
    ISUPPZ, strideISUPPZ, offsetISUPPZ,
    nrminv,
    resid,
    rqcorr,
    WORK, strideWork, offsetWork
) → Int32Array
```

Computes the (scaled) `r`-th column of the inverse of the submatrix in rows `b1` through `bn` of the tridiagonal matrix `L*D*L^T - lambda*I`.

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | order of the matrix |
| `b1` | `integer` | in |  |  | (1-based) first index of the submatrix |
| `bn` | `integer` | in |  |  | (1-based) last index of the submatrix |
| `lambda` | `number` | in |  |  | shift (approximate eigenvalue) |

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `dlar1v()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`DLAR1V`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/dlar1v.f).
-   This routine is a helper for `dstemr` and `dstegr`. When `lambda` is
    close to an eigenvalue of the submatrix, the returned vector is an
    unnormalized eigenvector.
-   `r` is in/out: pass `0` to let the routine pick the best twist index
    automatically; pass a nonzero 1-based value to force that twist.
-   All scalar outputs (`negcnt`, `ztz`, `mingma`, `r`, `nrminv`, `resid`,
    `rqcorr`) are written to caller-supplied length-1 typed arrays.

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import Int32Array from '@stdlib/array/int32/lib/index.js';
import dlar1v from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dlar1v';

const n = 5;
const td = [ 4.0, 4.0, 4.0, 4.0, 4.0 ];
const te = [ 1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0 ];

const D = new Float64Array( n );
const L = new Float64Array( n );
const LD = new Float64Array( n );
const LLD = new Float64Array( n );
const Z = new Float64Array( n );
const WORK = new Float64Array( 4 * n );
const ISUPPZ = new Int32Array( 2 );
const negcnt = new Int32Array( 1 );
const ztz = new Float64Array( 1 );
const mingma = new Float64Array( 1 );
const r = new Int32Array( 1 );
const nrminv = new Float64Array( 1 );
const resid = new Float64Array( 1 );
const rqcorr = new Float64Array( 1 );
let i;

D[ 0 ] = td[ 0 ];
for ( i = 0; i < n - 1; i += 1 ) {
	L[ i ] = te[ i ] / D[ i ];
	D[ i + 1 ] = td[ i + 1 ] - ( L[ i ] * te[ i ] );
	LD[ i ] = L[ i ] * D[ i ];
	LLD[ i ] = L[ i ] * L[ i ] * D[ i ];
}

const lambda = 4.0 - Math.sqrt( 3.0 );

dlar1v( n, 1, n, lambda, D, 1, L, 1, LD, 1, LLD, 1, 1e-300, 0.0, Z, 1, true, negcnt, ztz, mingma, r, ISUPPZ, 1, nrminv, resid, rqcorr, WORK ); // eslint-disable-line max-len

console.log( Z ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( 'r =', r[ 0 ], 'ztz =', ztz[ 0 ] ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DLAR1V`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DLAR1V computes the (scaled) r-th column of the inverse of the sumbmatrix in rows `B1` through `BN` of the tridiagonal matrix L D $L^T - \sigma$ I. When $\sigma$ is close to an eigenvalue, the computed vector is an accurate eigenvector. Usually, r corresponds to the index where the eigenvector is largest in magnitude. The following steps accomplish this computation : (a) Stationary qd transform, L D $L^T - \sigma$ $I = L(+)$ `D(+)` $L(+)^T$, (b) Progressive qd transform, L D $L^T - \sigma$ $I = U(-)$ `D(-)` $U(-)^T$, (c) Computation of the diagonal elements of the inverse of

-   L D $L^T - \sigma$ I by combining the above transforms, and choosing
-   r as the index where the diagonal of the inverse is (one of the)
-   largest in magnitude.

(d) Computation of the (scaled) r-th column of the inverse using the

-   twisted factorization obtained by combining the top part of the
-   the stationary and the bottom part of the progressive transform.

</section>
